voice: The singer, Ḍombīpāda, calls to Ḍombī the ferrywoman to row on because it has grown late, admires how she takes people across for nothing, and ends with a jab at those who climbed into chariots. The register is a plain rowing song: short commands, a refrain that works as a rowing call ('hey' for the particle lo), and no Dharma words; Munidatta's hearing of the refrain as the singer calling himself Ḍombī stays in the notes.

lines.en: Between the [Gaṅgā]{pl-ganga} and the [Yamunā]{pl-yamuna} a [boat]{boat} moves along.
Sunk there, the [Mātaṅgī]{matangi} lightly ferries the young one [across]{para}.
Row, Ḍombī, row, hey Ḍombī: it's grown late on the way.
By the true [guru]{guru}'s feet I'll go to the [city of the Jina]{jinapura} again.
Five [oars]{keruala} dipping at the prow, the rope tied at the stern,
bail out the water with the [sky]{gagana}-scoop; it doesn't get in at the seams.
Not looking to the two ways, left and right, row at will.
She takes no [cowrie]{kabadi}, takes no coin, she freely ferries [across]{para}.
Those who climbed onto a chariot can't row: they sink at [shore]{kula-shore} after [shore]{kula-shore}.

couplets.kept: Keeps both rivers, the boat and the paradox of a sunken ferrywoman. 'Sunk' (same reading as 'immersed') chimes with 'sink' in 5b, as buṛilī with buṛai; 'ferries across' ends the line, as pāra karei does here and in 5a.
couplets.letGo: The source couplet is unrhymed; the English adds only a light along/across echo from the plain words. 'With ease' becomes 'lightly' to keep the line end on 'across'. The doubtful poiālīle stays as the accurate draft divides it.

couplets.kept: Keeps the doubled call 'Row, Ḍombī', singing the particle lo of bāhalo as 'hey'. Moving 'again' to the end gives way/again, a near rhyme answering -chārā/-ṇaurā, with 'hey' chiming inside. Keeps the guru's feet rather than 'grace'.
couplets.letGo: 'It has grown late' contracts to 'it's grown late'. Way/again is a full rhyme only where 'again' is said to rhyme with 'rain'; elsewhere it is a slant rhyme.

couplets.kept: Keeps every part of the boat in the source's order: five oars, prow, stern, rope, sky-scoop, seams. 'Stern' and 'seams' share an opening s and a nasal close, a faint stand-in for the rhyme bāndhī/sāndhi.
couplets.letGo: The full rhyme bāndhī/sāndhi. 'Tied'/'inside' was possible only by fronting 'at the seams' and stretching 'in', so I let it go. 'With' and 'and' drop from 3a.

couplets.kept: Keeps 'two wheels'/'two ways' for the repeated dui, and 'row' from the refrain for bāhatu. 'At will' for chandā lets 'will' echo the stressed -lin- of 'pulinda', as -lindā and -chandā chime in the source.
couplets.letGo: 'As you please' becomes 'at will', and the articles before moon and sun drop. The source order and bare apposition stay, so the line decides nothing about what the pulinda is or does.

couplets.kept: Keeps the doubled 'takes no', the cowrie, and 'ferries across' at the line end as in 1b; 'freely' holds both senses of succhaṛe. 'Row' returns from the refrain, 'sink' from 1b, and 'shore after shore' keeps the doubling kulem̐ kula.
couplets.letGo: Unrhymed, as the source is. No self-naming is sung, because the Bengali couplet names no one (see questions).

questions: Couplet 5 is marked as the self-naming, but the Bengali names no one. The Tibetan translation (Toh 2293) reads 'Dom+bi 'gron bu mi len' ('Ḍombī takes no cowrie') in 5a, and in 5b 'gang zhig de la zhugs nas' ('whoever has entered it'), with no chariot. Should the Tibetan's 'Ḍombī' count as the bhaṇitā? I followed the Bengali and the accurate English ('She', 'chariot').

Refrain: I sang the particle lo in bāhalo as 'hey' ('row, hey Ḍombī'); the accurate English leaves it out. If the refrain should match the accurate English word for word, drop 'hey', and the cue becomes 'Row, Ḍombī, row, Ḍombī'.

1b: I sang 'sunk' for buṛilī where the accurate English has 'immersed', so that it echoes 'sink' (buṛai) in 5b, as the accurate draft's own flag suggests. Should the accurate English also take 'sunk', so the two versions agree?
1b: 'lightly' stands for līle ('with ease', as play). If you hear it as a different sense, 'with ease' can return at the line end, at the cost of the matching 'across' line ends in 1b and 5a.
